additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states 'הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת הֵם נֵרוֹת' — the mitzvot ARE candles. This is a bechina equation: mitzvot and candles share the same essential nature (both illuminate, both enable searching/discovery). The Rebbe anchors this in the verse 'נֵר מִצְוָה' (Proverbs 6:23), introduced with 'בִּבְחִינַת: נֵר מִצְוָה.' The mitzvah IS a candle — not that it produces a candle, but that it is one. מצוות belongs to the proposed Package 1 (the Candle/Soul cluster) alongside נרות and נשמה.
additions.source_quote: וְהַנֵּרוֹת נַעֲשִׂין מִן הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת כַּנַּ"ל, בִּבְחִינַת: נֵר מִצְוָה

additions.reason: נרות (candles) is the central linking concept of Torah #275. The Rebbe equates them with מצוות via 'הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת הֵם נֵרוֹת' and with the soul via the verse 'נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם'. The candle is not merely something the mitzvah produces — the mitzvah IS a candle (bechina, not eitza). Likewise, the soul IS God's candle (bechina). נרות sits at the center of the bechina cluster: נשמה ↔ נרות ↔ מצוות.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת הֵם נֵרוֹת שֶׁעַל־יָדָם הַחִפּוּשׂ כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: The verse 'נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם' (Proverbs 20:27) is cited by the Rebbe as the scriptural grounding for the bechina that souls and candles are the same thing: the soul of a person IS God's candle. The Rebbe uses this verse as a bechina proof — the soul searches (חוֹפֵשׂ) through inner chambers using candle-light. This is the same bechina structure as all the other 'נֵר מִצְוָה' equations: נשמה shares the essential nature of נר. נשמת אדם belongs in Package 1 as a third node in the candle-cluster alongside נרות and מצוות.
additions.source_quote: וְלָמְדוּ מִפָּסוּק: נֵר ה' נִשְׁמַת אָדָם חוֹפֵשׂ כָּל חַדְרֵי בָטֶן

additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states 'חָפְשִׁי, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הַחִפּוּשׂ שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה מִן הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת' — the word חָפְשִׁי (freedom from mitzvot after death, derived from Shabbat 151b interpreting Psalms 88:6) IS a bechina of the searching (חִפּוּשׂ). The Rebbe equates these two concepts: being free from mitzvot and being engaged in the candle-search are two faces of the same reality. חָפְשִׁי belongs in a proposed Package 2 alongside חִפּוּשׂ. Note: this 2-node cluster is borderline for an independent package; see the merge discussion in torah_275_new_packages.json.
additions.source_quote: חָפְשִׁי, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הַחִפּוּשׂ שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה מִן הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת, כִּי הַמִּצְוו‍ֹת הֵם נֵרוֹת שֶׁעַל־יָדָם הַחִפּוּשׂ כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: חִפּוּשׂ (searching/investigation in the Divine treasuries) is the explicit bechina-partner of חָפְשִׁי. The Rebbe states: 'חָפְשִׁי, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הַחִפּוּשׂ' — freedom-after-death and the act of searching are the same essential reality. Furthermore, the Torah opens by identifying searching in the King's treasury as 'תַּכְלִית כָּל תַּעֲנוּגֵי עוֹלָם הַבָּא' (the ultimate pleasure of the World to Come). חִפּוּשׂ is the central positive concept of the teaching.

analysis_notes.structural_notes: Torah #275 is a very short teaching (4 paragraphs, ~200 words). Despite its brevity, it contains substantive bechina language. The teaching's conceptual spine is: mitzvot-as-candles enable the soul's post-mortem searching in the Divine treasury — this is the ultimate World-to-Come pleasure. The Rebbe grounds this in two bechina equations: (1) מצוות = נרות = נשמה (the 'candle cluster'), and (2) חָפְשִׁי = חִפּוּשׂ (the 'freedom-as-searching' bechina). The Torah's eitza flow is: perform mitzvot → candles created → soul uses candles to search in ganzei Melech → ultimate pleasure. The bechina equations identify WHAT the candles essentially ARE (identical to the mitzvot and the soul) and WHAT the freedom-after-death essentially IS (identical to the searching). None of Torah 275's concepts appear in torahData.js under reference 275 — the entire Torah is unentered in the dataset.
